results.name: What's the Latest Version of Android?
results.content:
### Summary  
- Android 16 is the most recent version of Android. It was released on June 10, 2025.  
Android can be confusing. There are a lot of different versions, and many of them are still running on devices today. Keeping up with the latest version can be a challenge, and you may need [a new Android phone](https://www.howtogeek.com/734936/best-android-phones/) to get the latest and greatest version of Android.  
Major Android versions are generally released once per year (though it wasn't always like this), with monthly security updates released in between. Occasionally, Google also releases point updates (.1, .2, etc.), though those generally come without regularity. Oftentimes, more significant updates that aren't quite as significant as full version releases warrant a point update—like the update from Android 8.0 to Android 8.1, for example.  
For many years, every version of Android came with a dessert nickname, which many people used instead of the version number. However, Google ended that practice in 2019 with Android 10.
## The Latest Version of Android is 16  
Android 16 is the latest version of Android, and it was released on [June 10, 2025](https://www.howtogeek.com/android-16-june-pixel-drop-official/). It arrived first on Google Pixel phones and has [quickly rolled out](https://www.howtogeek.com/samsung-galaxy-one-ui-8-android-16-update-officially-begins/) to Samsung Galaxy devices as well. Phones from OnePlus, Xiaomi, Nokia, and others will eventually follow as well.  
Following in the tradition started with Android 10, Android 16 does not have a fun dessert nickname. However, the internal codename for the release is "Baklava." It doesn't start with "W," as you might expect, because Google started the lettering system over again with a new build process.  
Android 16 may not have a ton of big user-facing changes—[unless you use a Pixel phone](https://www.howtogeek.com/google-material-expressive-design/)—but there are plenty of little improvements. Some of the bigger features include [Live Updates](https://www.howtogeek.com/live-update-notifications-android-16/), [lock screen widgets](https://www.howtogeek.com/android-lock-screen-widgets-how-they-work/) (eventually), grouped notifications, a [better desktop mode](https://www.howtogeek.com/android-copying-samsung-dex-desktop-mode/), and much more.
## How to Update to the Latest Version of Android  
The short answer is also an unfortunate one: you might not be able to. The manufacturer of your phone first handles Android updates, so Samsung is responsible for its updates. The only updates handled by Google itself are for Pixel devices.  
To see if there's an update available for your device, head into Settings > System > System Update (or similar). Again, this may be in a different place depending on your phone—Samsung puts the System Updates option in the root of the Settings menu (Settings > Software Update > Download and Install), for example.  
Tapping this option will check for an update on the device, but there's a good chance it won't find anything. As soon as an update is available for your phone, it generally notifies you of that fact and prompts you to download and install it right then.  
The only surefire way to make sure you'll get the latest version of Android is to [buy from the Pixel line](https://www.howtogeek.com/336133/if-you-want-android-just-buy-googles-pixel-phone/). Google updates these phones directly, and they're generally up to date with the latest major version and security patches.

results.name: Android 16 - All the New Features of Our Latest Update Version | Android
results.content:
## **What is the latest Android version? Android 16 explained.**  
The latest Android version is Android 16.  
With each release, Android is committed to improving your experience. From enhanced accessibility to strengthened security, we're always working to make your Android-powered device even better.
## **How do I update to Android 16?**  
In most cases, your Android device will update automatically, so you don’t need to do anything. The latest version will simply install in the background when it’s ready.  
However, you can also manually check your current version or see whether Android 16 is available on your device.  
1. Open Settings
2. Tap About phone or About tablet > Android version
3. View your “Android version”  
Get more information on [how to manually check and install the latest Android updates](https://support.google.com/android/answer/15728187).
## **What’s the difference between Android 15 and 16?**  
Android 16 builds on the core capabilities of Android 15 with new features and updates.  
With Android 16 features like custom keyboard shortcuts and desktop windowing, the latest Android version makes using your device easier than ever. Added security updates keep you in control of your data, and accessibility enhancements put everything you need right at your fingertips, making your Android-powered device even more powerful.

results.name: What Version of Android Do I Have?
results.content:
### Summary  
To check the Android version on your device, go to Settings > About Phone > Android Version. Samsung Galaxy users can go to Settings > About Phone > Software Information.  
Android phones and tablets aren't all running the same version of the operating system. You might want to know which version yours has in order to know which features are available. We'll show you how to check the [Android version](https://www.howtogeek.com/719851/the-10-greatest-versions-of-android-ranked/).
## How to Check What Android Version You Have  
On most Android phones and tablets, you can check the version by going to Settings > About Phone/Tablet > Android Version. Here's what that looks like on a Google Pixel.  
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen to reveal the full [Quick Settings panel](https://www.howtogeek.com/231078/use-android-6.0%e2%80%99s-hidden-system-ui-tuner-to-customize-your-quick-settings-and-status-bar/), then tap the gear icon.  
Scroll down and select "About Phone."  
Lastly, scroll all the way down to "Android Version." The version your device is running will be labeled underneath in smaller text---Android 13, in this case.  
For even more information, tap "Android Version" and you'll see the [monthly security update](https://www.howtogeek.com/711886/what-are-android-security-updates-and-why-are-they-important/) and [Google Play system update](https://www.howtogeek.com/686927/what-are-google-play-system-updates-on-android-and-are-they-important/) as well.  
That's all there is to it! Checking for updates is the easy part, [actually getting updates for your phone is not always so easy](https://www.howtogeek.com/129273/why-your-android-phone-isnt-getting-operating-system-updates-and-what-you-can-do-about-it/).
## What Is the Latest Android Version?  
We've shown you how to check which Android version is running on your device, but what is the current Android version? As of March 2023, the [latest version of Android is Android 13](https://www.howtogeek.com/345250/whats-the-latest-version-of-android/). It was released on August 15, 2023.  
Android 13 [does not have an official dessert nickname](https://www.howtogeek.com/867311/why-did-google-stop-using-android-dessert-names/), but it is referred to internally as "Tiramisu." The next version, Android 14, is slated for release in Fall 2024. Theinternal codename for Android 14 is "Upside Down Cake."  
Android updates can be a frustrating part of using an Android device. New features get announced and you're never sure if [your specific Android device](https://www.howtogeek.com/347761/how-to-find-out-what-model-of-android-phone-you-have/) will get them. Before [buying a new Android phone](https://www.howtogeek.com/734936/best-android-phones/), check out [which ones have the best support](https://www.howtogeek.com/797200/how-long-will-my-android-phone-be-supported-with-updates/).
